_note: Run: <torch-venv>/bin/python bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/igpt-backbone.json --python <torch-venv>/bin/python (an interpreter with torch/timm, so the frozen backbone builds and loads in-process; use an absolute path for --python). This is the A3:igpt wiring (docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md). iGPT is hand-written and non-timm, so -- like MAE and I-JEPA -- it ships its own downstream_backbone.py provider. It is the first provider whose input is not an image tensor: it quantises pixels to colour tokens and reads a middle transformer layer, so its provider absorbs two things the shared ViT schema has no slot for (the chosen A3:igpt shape): the colour vocabulary (inferred from encoder.pt) and the colour clusters (read from clusters.npy beside encoder.pt). These mutations prove the wiring's guards are not vacuous: the vocabulary is really inferred from the checkpoint, missing/mismatched clusters are refused, alien or missing encoder weights are refused, and the middle-layer tokens are reshaped to the grid faithfully (pooling the map reproduces iGPT's own probe feature).
